content.text: Right now my app is running fine at "https://phishsense.design/". The main page shows a Leaderboard on the left and the PhishSense Masters on the right. I would like for the data in these two places to be loaded from records stored in my database hosted in Vultr named "appdb" in the table "scores". Walk me through these changes
I'll start by looking at how the app is built and where the Leaderboard and Masters data come from now.

2	-- Paste this whole file into the Tiger Data SQL editor and run it once.

4	-- Table 1: every scenario (our 20 backups + whatever Gemini makes)
5	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scenarios (
6	  scenario_id  SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
7	  source       TEXT NOT NULL,              -- 'sheet' (backup) or 'gemini'
8	  channel      TEXT NOT NULL,              -- 'email' or 'sms'
9	  difficulty   TEXT NOT NULL,              -- 'easy', 'medium', 'hard'
10	  sender       TEXT NOT NULL,
11	  subject      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
12	  body         TEXT NOT NULL,
13	  link         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
14	  game_answer  TEXT NOT NULL,              -- 'Phish' or 'Legit'
15	  red_flags    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
16	  explanation  TEXT NOT NULL,
17	  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
18	);
19	
20	-- Table 2: the leaderboard
21	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scores (
22	  username     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
23	  total_score  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
24	  badges       TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
25	  updated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
26	);

1	# PhishSense 🎣
2	
3	**Don't get hooked.**
4	
5	PhishSense uses Gemini to create endless realistic scams, then reveals the red flags you missed. Learn to protect yourself by joining the club and level up from Minnow to Master.
6	
7	Built at **Emory Hacks 2026** by Abigail, Bryan, Ismahan, and Yusra.
8	
9	**Live site:** [phishsense-livid.vercel.app](https://phishsense-livid.vercel.app/)
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Why we built it
14	
15	Phishing is one of the most common ways attackers get in, but most security training is a slideshow people click through without learning anything. The same example emails get reused until everyone memorizes them. PhishSense turns training into a game that never repeats, so players build real instincts instead of memorizing answers.
16	
17	## How it works
18	
19	1. **Pick a mode:** Easy, Medium, or Hard. Each run is 5 rounds.
20	2. **Read the message:** an email or a text message at a fictional company, Bayline Energy.
21	3. **Make the call:** Phish or Legit?
22	4. **See the red flags:** right or wrong, the game explains what to catch, like lookalike domains, fake urgency, or a phone number that isn't the company's real line.
23	5. **Earn the badge:** get 4 of 5 right.
24	
25	| Mode | Badge | What you face |
26	|---|---|---|
27	| Easy | 🐟 Minnow | Obvious scams: prizes you never entered, typos, ALL CAPS urgency |
28	| Medium | 🎣 Angler | Realistic scams: lookalike domains, fake failed payments, fake company IT |
29	| Hard | ⚓ Captain | Subtle tricks like subdomains, plus real emails that only look scary |
30	| All three | 🏆 PhishSense Master | Earn every badge to top the leaderboard |
31	
32	## No sign-up, on purpose
33	
34	Players just enter a name and play. We don't collect emails, passwords, or any personal information. A security training app shouldn't create new data that needs protecting, and it means anyone can start learning in seconds.
35	
36	## Safe by design
37	
38	- **Fictional only:** every company, brand, and person in the game is made up. The company players "work at" is Bayline Energy (`@bayline-energy.com`, main line (404) 555-0100).
39	- **No real phone numbers:** every number uses the reserved 555-01xx range.
40	- **No live links:** links are shown as plain text and are never clickable.
41	- **No peeking:** the correct answer stays on the server until the player guesses.
42	- **No secrets in the code:** API keys and the database password live in a `.env` file that is never committed.
43	
44	## How it's built
45	
46	| Piece | What it does |
47	|---|---|
48	| **Game screens** (`public/`) | HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Inbox-style emails and phone-style texts. |
49	| **Backend** (`server.js`) | Node.js and Express. Serves scenarios, checks answers, saves scores. |
50	| **Gemini API** | Writes a brand-new scenario every round, matched to the difficulty. |
51	| **Vultr** (PostgreSQL) | Stores scenarios and the leaderboard. |
52	| **Vercel** | Hosts the live site. |
53	| **Entire** | Our team's git workflow. |
54	
55	### Gemini + backup scenarios
56	
57	Every scenario lives in one `scenarios` table, with a `source` column:
58	
59	- `sheet`: 20 hand-written, hand-checked scenarios (8 Easy, 7 Medium, 5 Hard; 15 emails and 5 texts).
60	- `gemini`: new scenarios Gemini writes during play, saved automatically.
61	
62	When a round starts, the backend asks Gemini for a new scenario and shows it two of our backups as style examples. If Gemini is slow (over 6 seconds) or fails, the game quietly uses a backup instead, so players never see an error.
63	
64	## Run it yourself
65	
66	### Option 1: Practice mode (no setup)
67	Open `public/index.html` in a browser, or right-click it in VS Code and choose **Open with Live Server**. The game runs on the 20 backup scenarios, and the leaderboard saves in your browser.
68	
69	### Option 2: Full app (Gemini + database)
70	1. **Database:** create a Vultr Managed Database (PostgreSQL). Connect to it with a SQL tool such as psql or pgAdmin, using the connection details from Vultr, then run `setup.sql`. The last result should show easy 8, hard 5, medium 7.
71	2. **Keys:** copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in:
72	   - `DATABASE_URL`: your Vultr database connection string
73	   - `GEMINI_API_KEY`: from Google AI Studio
74	   - `GEMINI_MODEL`: the current Gemini Flash model name
75	3. **Run:** `npm install`, then `npm start`, and open http://localhost:3000
76	
77	The full app also works without a Gemini key. It just uses the backup scenarios.
78	
79	### API routes
80	
81	| Route | What it does |
82	|---|---|
83	| `GET /api/scenario?mode=easy` | Returns a message (Gemini first, backup if needed). Never includes the answer. |
84	| `POST /api/answer` | `{ scenario_id, guess }` returns whether it was right, the red flags, and the explanation. |
85	| `POST /api/score` | `{ username, points, badge }` saves a finished run. |
86	| `GET /api/leaderboard` | Top 50 players. |
87	
88	## Project files
89	
90	```
91	phish-sense/
92	  public/
93	    index.html      Game screens
94	    style.css       Look and feel
95	    app.js          Game logic
96	    mock-data.js    Backup scenarios for practice mode
97	    logo-badge.svg  Logo
98	  server.js         Backend
99	  setup.sql         Database setup + 20 backup scenarios
100	  .env.example      Template for keys (copy to .env)
101	```
102	
103	## What's next
104	
105	- **Accounts (optional):** save progress across devices, without collecting more data than needed.
106	- **Scam Library:** search every scenario and red flag instantly, typos and all, powered by Typesense.
107	- **More formats:** QR code phishing, voicemail transcripts, and fake login pages.
108	- **Team mode:** let companies run phishing training with their own dashboards.
109	- **Personal practice:** focus each player on the red flags they miss most.

117	| Ismahan | Database setup |

content.text:
Your site was already set up to read the Leaderboard and Masters from `scores`, but that connection is broken on the live server. I've fixed the code on `Connect_to_DB`. The other half is configuring the server to use `appdb`, which only you can do because it needs access to the Vultr server and console.

## What's actually happening on the live site

`https://phishsense.design/` loads fine, but every `/api/*` call, including `/api/leaderboard`, returns **502 Bad Gateway**. When that check fails, the front end switches to practice mode without telling anyone, and the two panels read from that visitor's own browser storage (`localStorage`). Each visitor sees only their own scores, and nothing goes into the database.

The likely cause is that the server's database setting (`DATABASE_URL`) is missing, wrong, or points to a database without the tables. When a query fails, Express 4 doesn't catch the error, so Node crashes and nginx shows 502. I haven't confirmed this; step 3 below shows you the exact error.

## Part 1: Code changes (done, not committed)

**`server.js`**
- **New `safe()` wrapper on every route:** a database error now returns a clean 500 instead of crashing the app. I tested this locally with a database that couldn't be reached: both API calls returned 500, the server stayed up, and the log showed `GET /api/masters failed: ECONNREFUSED`.
- **New `GET /api/masters`:** returns players whose `badges` contain all of `easy`, `medium` and `hard`, highest score first. Before, the Masters list was filtered out of the top 50 leaderboard rows, so a Master ranked below 50 would have been missed.
- **Other small fixes:** a dropped database connection no longer kills the process, and the scenario route handles an empty scenarios table.

**`public/app.js`**
- **Practice mode only when there's no backend:** `checkBackend()` now switches only when there's no backend at all (network error or 404). If the server answers with a 500 or 502, the site stays online.
- **Each panel loads from its own endpoint:** the Leaderboard from `/api/leaderboard` and the Masters from `/api/masters`, at the same time.
- **Errors are visible:** if a panel fails to load, it shows "Couldn't load scores right now" instead of browser-only data.

Your editor may still flag a "`)` expected" error in `server.js`. That warning is out of date: `node --check` passes on every file.

## Part 2: Point the server at `appdb` (you do this)

**1. Get the connection string.** In the Vultr console, go to Databases, open your database, and find Connection Details. Build this:
```
postgresql://vultradmin:<password>@<host>.vultrdb.com:<port>/appdb
```
Leave off any `?sslmode=require` at the end. `server.js` already turns on SSL, and with that suffix the `pg` driver tries to fully verify Vultr's certificate. That would probably fail with a "self-signed certificate" error.

**2. Allow the app server to connect.** On the database's Settings page, under Trusted Sources, add your app server's IP address (or put both in the same VPC). If you also want to test from your PC, add your own IP too.

**3. Make sure the tables exist in `appdb`.** Connect with psql or pgAdmin and run:
```sql
\d scores
```
- **If the table is missing:** run the whole `setup.sql`. It's safe to re-run, and the game also needs the `scenarios` table it creates.
- **If the table already exists:** check that it has `username` (unique), `total_score` (integer), `badges` (text array) and `updated_at`. If the columns are different, send me the output and I'll adjust the queries.

**4. Update the server's `.env` and restart.** SSH into the server:
```bash
sudo nano /var/www/phish-sense/.env      # set DATABASE_URL=... from step 1
sudo systemctl restart phishsense
sudo journalctl -u phishsense -n 30 --no-pager
```
The log line should say `PhishSense running...`, with no errors after it. If something is wrong, this log now shows the reason.

**5. Check it.** This should return JSON (`[]` if the table is empty), not a 502:
```bash
curl https://phishsense.design/api/leaderboard
curl https://phishsense.design/api/masters
```

## Part 3: Ship the code

Commit on `Connect_to_DB`, open a PR, and merge it to `main`. Your GitHub Actions workflow will deploy it. Its health check only loads the homepage, so do step 5 yourself after the deploy.

Scores players earned on the live site so far exist only in their own browsers. They can't be moved into the database, so the boards will start from whatever is already in `appdb`.

- **Your app server's IP:** required, or the live site can never connect.

**3. Set it on the server and restart:**

- name: Clean up key
        if: always()
        run: rm -f ~/.ssh/id_deploy

  # This workflow runs on push to main (not a pull_request event), so

  comment-on-pr:
    needs: deploy
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04

      pull-requests: write

        id: pr-production-comment
        with:
          issue-number: ${{ steps.find-pr.outputs.number }}

            💻 Commit SHA: ${{ github.sha }}

            - Your changes have been pushed to production and are now live.
            - Future merges to `main` will redeploy the live site automatically.

            > *This is an automated message.*
          reactions: "rocket"

content.text:
I added a new job, `comment-on-pr`, to `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`. It runs only after the `deploy` job succeeds, so a failed deploy never posts a "live" comment. I haven't run it or committed it yet. I also couldn't run a YAML syntax check because the tool for it was blocked here, so GitHub will flag any formatting problem when you push.

**It works differently from your template in two ways:**
- **It looks up the PR number.** Your workflow runs when code is pushed to `main`, so `github.event.pull_request.number` would be empty. The job asks GitHub which PR the merged commit came from. If there isn't one, such as a manual run, it skips the comment instead of failing.
- **It uses `@v4` instead of `@v3`.** v3 runs on Node 16, which GitHub has retired for Actions. The inputs (`issue-number`, `body`, `reactions`) are the same.

**The comment it posts:**
```
### WebApp Production Deployment
🔗 Live site: https://phishsense.design/
💻 Commit SHA: <merged commit SHA>

- Your changes have been pushed to production and are now live.
- Future merges to `main` will redeploy the live site automatically.

> *This is an automated message.*
```
It also adds the 🚀 reaction. The SHA is the commit that was actually deployed to `main`.

The job gives itself permission to write PR comments, so you don't need a token or a new secret. If GitHub still refuses to post the comment, go to repo Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions and make sure it isn't blocking write access for workflows.

You'll see the first comment on the PR that merges this change.
